title: opt-in-response-contract-mode-and-stream-checkpointing-with-toolcall-fencing
author: Marina Lopez
description: Context: Customers need a gradual opt-in for stricter JSON-based response contracts while preserving streaming stability and OpenAI compatibility. This PR introduces a route-level response_contract opt-in (response_contract.mode = "opt_in_strict") that enables a stricter validation pass during streaming and a lightweight runtime checkpointing mechanism so streams can rewind to the last validated checkpoint if validation fails. Motivation: avoid a hard breaking switch across the fleet; allow teams to enable stronger guarantees per-route and keep tool/function-calling safe under streaming validation. Key ideas: 1) opt-in strict mode toggles additional validation checkpoints at schema-boundary tokens, not every token, to limit latency impact. 2) When a checkpoint fails validation we surface a clear error with a rewind token and optionally attempt a best-effort correction path (off by default). 3) Tool/function calls are fenced: the runtime will not emit toolcall events to downstream tool runners unless the preceding schema fragment for the call is syntactically valid and an accept token is reached. 4) OpenAI compatibility layer: we map older function_call signals into the new fenced lifecycle and return legacy-style error objects for compatibility, plus telemetry context IDs for easier triage.
commit_summary: runtime: add ResponseContractMode enum and route-level opt-in flag
streaming: implement checkpointing slab and rewind token generation
validator: incremental JSONSchema boundary validator with token anchoring
tooling: fence function_call emission until schema-validated checkpoint
compat: adapter to translate legacy function_call into fenced lifecycle and error mapping
console: UI toggle + telemetry fields for response contract opt-in
tests: unit + integration + e2e for stream rewind, fencing and compat mapping
review_thread: Arjun Patel: Can we clarify how checkpoint frequency is derived? Request: add docs comment and a unit test covering average 1 checkpoint per ~256 tokens for typical prompts.

Marina Lopez (author): Added a comments block and a new unit test (runtime/tests/checkpoint_freq.test.rs). Checkpoint frequency is heuristic: min(1, sequence_len/256) with safeguards for very short sequences.
Sophie Nguyen: Behavioural Q: when fencing prevents a tool call, how does the user get the tool execution result? Suggest fallback path description in docs and a clear error code.

Marina Lopez: If fencing prevents emission we return a 409-like structured error (code: RESPONSE_CONTRACT_UNSAFE_TOOLCALL) with a rewind token. Docs updated with fallback narrative and example payload.
Derek Holt: CI flake on e2e test observed. Reran pipeline; all green. Also asked to ensure backwards compatibility for existing OpenAI-style consumers.

Marina Lopez: Adapter added (adapters/openai_compat/adapter.go) that maps legacy function_call fields to the fenced lifecycle and surfaces legacy error objects under the legacy compatibility header. Added integration test openai_compat/toolcall_legacy.test.ts
release_notes: Introduce opt-in response contract mode that performs schema-bound checkpoints during streaming; adds stream rewind token when validation fails; tool/function-call fencing to avoid unsafe tool execution; OpenAI compat adapter maps legacy function_call semantics and returns backward-compatible error payloads. Opt-in only; no global breaking change.
error_codes: RESPONSE_CONTRACT_VALIDATION_ERROR - validation failed at checkpoint (includes rewind_token)
RESPONSE_CONTRACT_UNSAFE_TOOLCALL - tool call suppressed because pre-call fragment failed validation
RESPONSE_CONTRACT_RESUME_TOKEN_INVALID - provided resume token not found in current routing shard
operational_notes: Runtime will emit telemetry field response_contract.context_id for every request when opt-in is enabled. When rewind_token is returned the console displays a Rewind button which triggers a re-request with resume_token header. Default behaviour: no automatic retry; operators can enable best_effort_autorepair in route config.
migration_guide: 1) Add response_contract.mode = "opt_in_strict" to desired routes. 2) Monitor telemetry: response_contract.validation_rate and response_contract.rewind_rate. 3) If many rewinds observed, consider increasing max_prefix_tolerance or enabling best_effort_autorepair for the route. 4) For OpenAI consumers, no change is required; adapter will translate error shapes automatically. See docs/migration/opt_in_strict_mode.md for examples.
examples: Example error payload: {"error":{"code":"RESPONSE_CONTRACT_VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Schema validation failed at 'result.items[0].id'","rewind_token":"rw_abc123:shard-7-159"}}

Example fence behaviour: streaming chunk that completes a function_call object is held in runtime buffer until checkpoint validated; if valid -> emit event AND run tool; if invalid -> emit error + rewind_token and do not run tool.
